Conditional moments of a GAM response distribution

Source: R/moments.R
conditional_moments.Rd

Construct covariate combinations using conditional_values() conventions, then estimate response moments with fitted_moments(). Other covariates are held at typical values; observations are not averaged over those covariates.

Usage

conditional_moments(
  model,
  condition = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  moments = c("mean", "variance", "cv"),
  n_vals = 100,
  complete = TRUE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'gam'
conditional_moments(
  model,
  condition = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  moments = c("mean", "variance", "cv"),
  n_vals = 100,
  complete = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

model

a fitted GAM object.

condition

either a character vector or a list supplying the names of covariates, and possibly their values, to condition up. The order of the values determines how these are plotted via the draw.conditional_values() method; the first element is mapped to the x channel, the second element to the colour channel, the third to ggplot2::facet_wrap() if no fourth element is present, if present, the fourth element is mapped to the rows and the third element is mapped to the columns of ggplot2::facet_grid().

data

optional data frame used to generate condition values and determine covariate classes. Explicit values in condition take precedence. Other covariates use the fitted model's typical values. The rows of data are not used directly as a prediction grid.

moments

Character vector selecting "mean", "variance", "sd", "cv", "skewness", "kurtosis", or "excess_kurtosis". "all" requests all seven. CV is SD divided by a strictly positive mean; kurtosis is the fourth central moment divided by squared variance.

n_vals

numeric; number of values to generate for numeric variables named in condition.

complete

logical; if TRUE (the default), retain all combinations of conditions. If FALSE, retain only combinations of factor levels among the variables named in condition that occur in the fitted model's data. Numeric conditions are not filtered, and variables absent from condition remain at their typical values. Supplied data does not change which combinations count as observed. An error is raised if no combinations remain.

...

Arguments to fitted_moments(), including uncertainty, nuisance, n_draws, seed, scores, and exclude.

Value

A tibble of class "conditional_moments", with the columns returned by fitted_moments() and the plotting channels of conditional_values().

Examples

library("mgcv")
m <- gam(mpg ~ s(wt, k = 5), data = mtcars, method = "REML")
conditional_moments(m, condition = "wt", moments = c("mean", "variance")) |>
  draw()
